description: ESP-r is a dynamic building performance simulation program developed by an international consortium led from the University of Strathclyde's Energy Systems Research Unit and supported by a user mailing list. Its simulation engine (bps) writes a binary results database that a separate tool (res) post-processes, and can also export XML and CSV when the libxml2 library is available. It installs from source with an Install script, preferably on Linux, and has also been built on Cygwin, MSYS2 and macOS; a precompiled Ubuntu 18.04 installation is offered from ESRU. The repository's version file reads V13.3.15 of 14 October 2022, and its latest commit, adding a Dockerfile, is from 4 February 2023. Coverage: generic. Access: free source and binaries. Licence: GNU GPL version 2 or later. Caveats: installation expects a writable /opt/esp-r directory and compiler set-up, and the ESRU site was not reachable here. Simulation uses: detailed thermal, energy and plant simulation of buildings. Related records: EnergyPlus and obFMU.
